MODNAME := lstp
KOFILE  := $(MODNAME).ko

UNAME_R := $(shell uname -r)
NPROC   := $(shell nproc 2>/dev/null || echo 1)

KDIR ?= /lib/modules/$(UNAME_R)/build
SRC_DIR := $(abspath $(dir $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))
BUILD   := $(SRC_DIR)/build
KO_PATH := $(BUILD)/$(KOFILE)

SOURCES := Kbuild $(filter-out %.mod.c,$(notdir $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/*.c) $(wildcard $(SRC_DIR)/*.h)))

KERNEL_SRC := $(HOME)/linux
UNAME_M := $(shell uname -m)
ifeq ($(UNAME_M),aarch64)
  ARCH ?= arm64
  CROSS_COMPILE ?= aarch64-linux-gnu-
else ifeq ($(UNAME_M),x86_64)
  ARCH ?= x86_64
  CROSS_COMPILE ?=
else ifeq ($(UNAME_M),armv7l)
  ARCH ?= arm
  CROSS_COMPILE ?= arm-linux-gnueabihf-
endif
ifdef DEBUG
  EXTRA_CFLAGS += -DDEBUG
endif

obj-m += $(MODNAME).o

# Pass command-line name=value pairs to insmod; unknown names fail at insmod time.
_MAKE_VARS := MODNAME KOFILE UNAME_R NPROC KDIR SRC_DIR BUILD KO_PATH SOURCES \
              KERNEL_SRC UNAME_M ARCH CROSS_COMPILE DEBUG EXTRA_CFLAGS obj-m \
              MODPARAMS _MAKE_VARS V W O KBUILD_VERBOSE
MODPARAMS ?= $(strip $(foreach v,$(.VARIABLES),\
  $(if $(filter command line,$(origin $(v))),\
    $(if $(filter $(v),$(_MAKE_VARS)),,$(v)=$($(v))))))

.PHONY: default build build_rpi clean clean_rpi reload install uninstall unload load

default build:
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD) && for f in $(SOURCES); do cp -p $(SRC_DIR)/$$f $(BUILD)/$$f; done
	@$(MAKE) -j$(NPROC) -C $(KDIR) M=$(BUILD) modules EXTRA_CFLAGS="$(EXTRA_CFLAGS)"; rc=$$?; for f in $(SOURCES); do rm -f $(BUILD)/$$f; done; exit $$rc

build_rpi:
	@mkdir -p $(BUILD) && for f in $(SOURCES); do cp -p $(SRC_DIR)/$$f $(BUILD)/$$f; done
	@$(MAKE) -j$(NPROC) -C $(KERNEL_SRC) ARCH=$(ARCH) CROSS_COMPILE=$(CROSS_COMPILE) M=$(BUILD) modules EXTRA_CFLAGS="$(EXTRA_CFLAGS)"; rc=$$?; for f in $(SOURCES); do rm -f $(BUILD)/$$f; done; exit $$rc

clean clean_rpi:
	rm -rf $(BUILD)

reload: unload build load

install: build
	@sudo mkdir -p /lib/modules/$(UNAME_R)/extra/
	@sudo cp $(KO_PATH) /lib/modules/$(UNAME_R)/extra/
	@sudo depmod -a
	@lsmod | grep -q '^$(MODNAME) ' || sudo modprobe $(MODNAME)

uninstall: unload
	@sudo rm -f /lib/modules/$(UNAME_R)/extra/$(KOFILE)
	@sudo depmod -a

unload:
	@sudo rmmod $(MODNAME) 2>/dev/null || true
	@lsmod | grep $(MODNAME) || true

load:
	@sudo insmod $(KO_PATH) $(MODPARAMS)
	@lsmod | grep $(MODNAME) || true
	@sudo dmesg | tail -10

## Security

NVIDIA is dedicated to the security and trust of our software products and services, including all source code repositories managed through our organization.

If you need to report a security issue, please use the appropriate contact points outlined below. **Please do not report security vulnerabilities through GitHub.**

## Reporting Potential Security Vulnerability in an NVIDIA Product

To report a potential security vulnerability in any NVIDIA product:
- Web: [Security Vulnerability Submission Form](https://www.nvidia.com/object/submit-security-vulnerability.html)
- E-Mail: psirt@nvidia.com
  - We encourage you to use the following PGP key for secure email communication: [NVIDIA public PGP Key for communication](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/pgp-key)
  - Please include the following information:
    - Product/Driver name and version/branch that contains the vulnerability
    - Type of vulnerability (code execution, denial of service, buffer overflow, etc.)
    - Instructions to reproduce the vulnerability
    - Proof-of-concept or exploit code
    - Potential impact of the vulnerability, including how an attacker could exploit the vulnerability

While NVIDIA currently does not have a bug bounty program, we do offer acknowledgement when an externally reported security issue is addressed under our coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy. Please visit our [Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security/psirt-policies/) policies page for more information.

## NVIDIA Product Security

For all security-related concerns, please visit NVIDIA's Product Security portal at https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/security

# Repository Agent Instructions

These instructions apply to the whole repository.

## Driver Context

This is an out-of-tree Linux kernel driver for NVIDIA LSTP USB devices. Treat
USB URBs, locking, memory lifetime, sysfs/kobject lifetime, firmware nodes, and
subsystem registration as correctness-critical.

The driver must support ASIC, FPGA, and microcontroller-backed LSTP endpoints;
OpenBMC and Ubuntu-style hosts; dynamic firmware-reported channel discovery; and
static firmware-described configuration via device tree or ACPI. Do not narrow
any of those paths unless explicitly asked.

The LSTP protocol and userspace-visible interfaces are already deployed. Packet
formats, command/status values, channel types, names, sysfs hierarchy,
attributes, module parameters, device tree bindings, and device-node behavior
are compatibility surfaces. Extensions must remain backwards compatible with
existing firmware, device trees, scripts, and userspace tools.

## Kernel And Compatibility Work

When changing memory management, locking, lifetime, URB behavior, wait queues,
workqueues, IRQ handling, kobjects, sysfs, fwnodes, or subsystem registration,
verify the relevant kernel implementation directly. Prefer `$KERNEL_SRC`; else
use `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/build`; for compatibility failures, inspect the
specific kernel tree being tested. For high-risk lifetime or concurrency
changes, mention which kernel source paths or APIs were checked.

Prefer newer kernel APIs when they are safer or cleaner. If older supported
kernels lack them, isolate differences in a compatibility header instead of
spreading version checks through driver code.

## Wire-Bound Structures

Every struct that crosses the LSTP wire is `__packed` with `__le*`/`__be*`
on multi-byte fields and plain `u8` for byte fields (`__u*` is UAPI-only).
Convert via `cpu_to_le*()` / `le*_to_cpu()` at field access.

Field access through a `__packed`-struct pointer is alignment-safe; do not
double-wrap with `get_unaligned_le*()` (use those only on raw byte buffers).

Promote each opcode variant to a top-level
`<subsystem>_<operation>_(req|resp)` struct -- no anonymous-struct unions
over opcodes.

Anchor cross-file wire-size assumptions with `BUILD_BUG_ON` at the consumer,
e.g. `BUILD_BUG_ON(sizeof(struct lstp_header) + sizeof(*req) > LSTP_USB_EP_MIN_SIZE)`.

## Stack-Allocated Request/Response Conventions

Per-call request/response structs use designated initializers in their
declaration, scoped to the branch that uses them. Name the local plainly
(`req`, `resp`); the struct type already carries the subsystem prefix.

## Formatting

The repo ships a `.clang-format` at the root. Run `clang-format-19 -i` on every
`.c`/`.h` file you touch before staging the final commit, and before every
amend that adjusts touched lines. Hand-resolved conflicts and partial rewrites
routinely leave wrap points that no longer match the column limit; reviewers
flag the resulting drift even when the logic is fine.

Limit the format pass to the files this change actually touches -- do not
sweep unrelated source files in the same commit. For touch-only formatting on
changed lines against the parent commit,
`git clang-format --binary clang-format-19 HEAD~1` is also available.

%YAML 1.2
---
$schema: http://devicetree.org/meta-schemas/core.yaml#

title: NVIDIA LSTP UART Channel

description: |
  UART channel on an NVIDIA LSTP USB device.

  The LSTP UART channel registers as a Linux tty device (/dev/ttyLSTPN,
  where N is a dynamically allocated minor).  Baud rate, framing, parity,
  and flow-control settings are reported by the device firmware at probe
  time and cannot be changed at runtime — userspace termios hardware bits
  are silently preserved across stty(1) invocations.

  A DT node is optional.  When present, it is attached to the tty device
  so that udev rules can produce stable /dev/serial/by-* symlinks and so
  that serdev-attached child devices (Bluetooth, GNSS, NFC, etc.) can be
  enumerated as DT children.

properties:
  compatible:
    const: nvidia,lstp-uart

  reg:
    description: LSTP channel ID as reported by firmware.
    maxItems: 1

patternProperties:
  "^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9,-]*$":
    type: object
    description: |
      Optional serdev child device attached to this UART (e.g. Bluetooth
      HCI, GNSS module).  Enumerated by the serdev core when the tty is
      opened.
    additionalProperties: true

    properties:
      compatible:
        description: Compatible string for the serdev peripheral.

    required:
      - compatible

required:
  - compatible
  - reg

additionalProperties: false

examples:
  - |
    /* Bare UART exposed as /dev/ttyLSTPN */
    channel@5 {
        compatible = "nvidia,lstp-uart";
        reg = <5>;
    };
  - |
    /* UART with an attached serdev child */
    channel@5 {
        compatible = "nvidia,lstp-uart";
        reg = <5>;

        bluetooth {
            compatible = "brcm,bcm43438-bt";
            max-speed = <3000000>;
        };
    };

%YAML 1.2
---
$schema: http://devicetree.org/meta-schemas/core.yaml#

title: NVIDIA LSTP SPI Channel

description: |
  SPI bus master channel on an NVIDIA LSTP USB device.

  The LSTP SPI channel registers as a Linux SPI controller.  Child nodes
  describe SPI peripherals attached to each chip-select.  When a DT node
  is present, the SPI core auto-enumerates children; otherwise the driver
  falls back to board_info registration.

  The number of chip selects and bus speed are reported by the device
  firmware.  Up to 2 chip selects (CS0-CS1) are supported by the driver.

allOf:
  - $ref: /schemas/spi/spi-controller.yaml#

properties:
  compatible:
    const: nvidia,lstp-spi

  reg:
    description: LSTP channel ID as reported by firmware.
    maxItems: 1

  "#address-cells":
    const: 1

  "#size-cells":
    const: 0

patternProperties:
  "^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9,-]*@[0-9a-f]+$":
    type: object
    additionalProperties: true

    properties:
      compatible:
        description: Compatible string for the SPI peripheral device.

      reg:
        description: Chip-select number (0-1).
        minimum: 0
        maximum: 1

      spi-max-frequency:
        description: |
          Maximum SPI clock frequency in Hz.  Must not exceed the speed
          reported by the LSTP device firmware.

    required:
      - compatible
      - reg

required:
  - compatible
  - reg
  - "#address-cells"
  - "#size-cells"

unevaluatedProperties: false

examples:
  - |
    channel@1 {
        compatible = "nvidia,lstp-spi";
        reg = <1>;
        #address-cells = <1>;
        #size-cells = <0>;

        spidev@0 {
            compatible = "nvidia,lstp-spidev";
            reg = <0>;
            spi-max-frequency = <24000000>;
        };

        spidev@1 {
            compatible = "nvidia,lstp-spidev";
            reg = <1>;
            spi-max-frequency = <24000000>;
        };
    };

%YAML 1.2
---
$schema: http://devicetree.org/meta-schemas/core.yaml#

title: NVIDIA LSTP I2C Channel

description: |
  I2C bus master channel on an NVIDIA LSTP USB device.

  The LSTP I2C channel registers as a Linux I2C adapter.  Child nodes
  describe I2C peripherals on the bus and are auto-enumerated by the
  I2C core at probe time.

  Bus numbering is controlled via standard DT aliases (e.g.
  i2c20 = &channel_label).  Without an alias the I2C core assigns a
  dynamic bus number.

properties:
  compatible:
    const: nvidia,lstp-i2c

  reg:
    description: LSTP channel ID as reported by firmware.
    maxItems: 1

  "#address-cells":
    const: 1

  "#size-cells":
    const: 0

  clock-frequency:
    description: |
      I2C bus clock frequency in Hz.  Reserved for future use.
      Common values: 100000 (standard), 400000 (fast).
    default: 100000

  retries:
    description: |
      Number of times the I2C core re-issues a transfer that fails with
      -EAGAIN (arbitration loss or bus busy) before giving up.

      Ignored (forced to 0) when the channel config reports a non-zero
      bus_arbitration_retries value.  Such a device performs its own bus
      retries, covering both arbitration loss and bus-busy, before returning
      failure to the host, so no host-side retries are added on top.
    $ref: /schemas/types.yaml#/definitions/uint32
    maximum: 255
    default: 3

patternProperties:
  "^[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9,-]*@[0-9a-f]+$":
    type: object
    additionalProperties: true

    properties:
      compatible:
        description: Compatible string for the I2C peripheral.

      reg:
        description: I2C slave address.
        maxItems: 1

    required:
      - compatible
      - reg

required:
  - compatible
  - reg

additionalProperties: false

examples:
  - |
    /* Minimal: dynamic bus number, one child device */
    channel@2 {
        compatible = "nvidia,lstp-i2c";
        reg = <2>;
        #address-cells = <1>;
        #size-cells = <0>;
        retries = <5>;

        sensor@48 {
            compatible = "ti,tmp102";
            reg = <0x48>;
        };
    };
